image_description: A light blue minibus parked on a street with a person standing next to the open side door. The vehicle has a high roof, a front grille, and visible wheels. The background includes buildings and trees.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Boxy body shape noticeably shorter than a full-size bus, yet tall enough for passengers to stand or sit upright comfortably.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle exhibits a distinct boxy silhouette with a high roofline typical of passenger vans/minibuses, clearly shorter than a city bus.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large windshield and row of side windows along passenger area.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large front windshield is visible, and there are multiple side windows extending along the passenger cabin area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Height is substantial, with entrance door at front or mid-body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle height allows for upright entry (evidenced by the standing person), and the door is located at the mid-body position.
A door is visible in the open position on the side of the vehicle, consistent with a sliding or folding mechanism.
The front section of the vehicle features a grille and headlights, indicating a standard front-engine layout.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rear flat or slightly angled panel with taillights and license plate mount.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the vehicle is not visible in this angle; only the front three-quarters are shown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Standard van-sized wheels with steel or alloy rims.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible front wheel appears to be a standard size for a van/minibus with a hubcap/rim structure.
The window configuration and overall size suggest a capacity within the 4-10 passenger range.

The side mirror housing lacks defined structural edges and seems to blend into the door frame. The door handles appear slightly misaligned and lack sharp mechanical definition.
The vertical lines of the building in the background show slight warping, inconsistent with standard architectural perspective.
